title: security: under MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, moe-agent.sh/.ps1 run only a known agent CLI, resolved outside the project
description:
Split from task-465ee875 (HIGH, the PROTECTED agentCommand gap) by architect-4ae016fb on 2026-10-30. That row keeps three things and dependsOn this one: the JetBrains launcher slice, docs/CONFIGURATION.md, and the final verification of both slices.

Problem:
- scripts/moe-agent.sh parses --command into COMMAND_BIN plus COMMAND_ARGV (parse_command_into_argv, ~:366) and runs it. The basename only classifies the CLI as codex, gemini or grok; anything else counts as claude.
- moe-agent.ps1 Resolve-CommandParts (~:318) does the same with -Command.
- Under the PROTECTED profile, the IDE forwards a value that repository content can choose (.moe/project.json settings.agentCommand). The wrapper then runs a repository-chosen binary on the host.
- Under the threat model in docs/design/protected-profile-threat-model.md (CQ-RF05), a file under the project may add a refusal but never an admission.

Wanted, only when MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED is exactly '1' (the CQ-R13c1 marker; reuse CQ-R13c2's RUNTIME_PROTECTED flag once it lands):
- The command must be exactly one of claude, codex, gemini, grok: one bare token, with no path separator, no extension and no extra arguments.
- For anything else, print one stderr line, byte-identical in both wrappers, then exit 1. Do this before any MCP config write or daemon RPC:
  [ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMAND_REFUSED: '<command>' is not one of claude, codex, gemini, grok; the protected runtime runs only these agent CLIs by name. Refusing to start.
  Show the command as given, truncated to 200 characters, with control characters replaced.
- Resolve a known name only from absolute PATH entries outside the project. Drop empty entries, '.', relative entries, and entries under the project's real path. Every later invocation of that CLI by the wrapper, the account checks included, uses the resolved absolute path.
- If no such entry holds the CLI, print one line, MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND, naming the CLI, then exit 1.
- Without the marker, behavior is unchanged byte for byte (legacy policy).

Tests: a new scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs. Model it on CQ-R13c2's marker rows: sh rows, plus ps1 rows where PowerShell exists. Rows:
- refused: a path, 'claude --flag', 'claude.exe', and an empty value;
- accepted: 'codex' found on a trusted PATH dir;
- not run: a project-local ./claude reachable only through an empty, '.' or in-project PATH entry;
- unchanged: the same commands without the marker.
scripts/tests/parity-check.sh must pass, because the refusal strings are identical in both wrappers.

Ordering:
- This row dependsOn CQ-R13c2 (task-6f5cf10f), which adds the marker gate to the same two wrappers.
- moe-agent.sh/.ps1 are hot files. The planning architect must check every open row that edits them (CQ-V07, V08, V08b, V04c, task-e7f4026a, task-01f37ac6, task-a2f243a1, task-dfbda1a8) and serialize through dependsOn where hunks would collide.

Not in scope: the JetBrains launcher and the docs (task-465ee875), VS Code, and the daemon.
definitionOfDone: With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1, both wrappers refuse any --command/-Command that is not exactly claude, codex, gemini or grok. They print the byte-identical MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMAND_REFUSED line naming the command, exit 1, and make no daemon RPC or MCP config write. Proven by scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs rows for sh, and for ps1 where PowerShell exists.

With the marker, a known CLI runs only from an absolute PATH entry outside the project. A project-local binary reachable only through an empty, relative or in-project PATH entry is never run, and a missing CLI refuses with MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND. Without the marker, behavior is unchanged. Proven by the same test file.
`node --test scripts/tests/protected-agent-command.test.mjs` and `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` exit 0, with their output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Legacy policy is unchanged: every new branch runs only when MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED is exactly '1'.
The refusal lines are byte-identical in moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1, and moe-agent.ps1 stays UTF-8 with a BOM (scripts/CLAUDE.md).

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.sh. Under RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 only (R13c2's flag, which is set when MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED is exactly '1'):

1. Right after the command is parsed and the CLI type detected (CMD_FIRST and CMD_BASE, ~:416-440), and BEFORE any MCP config write or daemon RPC, add a helper protected_agent_command_gate. It accepts COMMAND only when the raw value is exactly one of claude, codex, gemini, grok (case-sensitive) and parse_command_into_argv produced no extra argv. Otherwise:
   - print the R1 line to stderr (`printf '%s\n'` with the sanitized value: tr -d control chars, then cut to 200 chars);
   - exit 1.
   Write it as an if/else: the file runs under set -e (mem:gotcha-moe-agent-sh-set-e-unguarded-assignments).
2. A helper protected_resolve_cli NAME:
   - Walk PATH split on ':'. Skip an empty entry, '.', any entry not starting with '/', and any entry whose `cd "$entry" && pwd -P` equals the project's real path or lies under it with a '/' boundary.
   - Return the first `$dir/$NAME` that is a regular executable file. On MSYS/MINGW (uname -s), also try `.exe` and `.cmd`.
   - Do a manual scan, not `command -v`: bash's hash table and aliases must not answer.
   - On success, set COMMAND_BIN to that absolute path and print the A1 INFO line. On failure, print the T1 CLI_NOT_FOUND line and exit 1.
   - Call it right after the gate.
3. COMMAND_BIN is re-parsed later (~:546 and ~:679 call parse_command_into_argv again after PYTHON_CMD resolves). Under the marker, re-apply the resolved absolute path after every such re-parse, so no later site ever sees the bare name. Any later name substitution (`gemini` -> `agy`, ~:7831) under the marker must also go through protected_resolve_cli, or be skipped. Compare on CMD_BASE, not COMMAND_BIN.

Error handling:
- every refusal is one stderr line and exit 1, with no partial state: nothing written, no RPC;
- a `cd` into an unreadable PATH entry fails quietly and that entry is skipped;
- the gate and the resolver never run without the marker.

Without the marker, every byte of behavior is unchanged. Run `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` before every save of a final version.
implementationPlan.note:
moe-agent.sh (marker-only, legacy bytes unchanged):
- refuse_protected_agent + allowlist gate right BEFORE CLI-type detection (earliest point; ahead of the prompt-cache check, which reads COMMAND_ARGV and project settings and could otherwise answer first). `case "$COMMAND" in claude|codex|gemini|grok)`; otherwise one plain stderr line, value shown as `${COMMAND//[[:cntrl:]]/?}` cut with `${:0:200}`, WORKER_ID cleared (EXIT trap deregisters nothing), exit 1.
- protected_resolve_cli right after R13c2's path gate (needs PROJECT): `IFS=: read -r -a` of PATH (no globbing), skips non-'/' entries (empty, '.', relative), `cd -- && pwd -P` (unreadable entry skipped), ancestor walk with `-ef` against the project's `pwd -P` (catches symlinks, '..' and case-insensitive spellings), first regular executable `$real/$name` (MSYS/MINGW/CYGWIN also .exe/.cmd). Sets COMMAND_BIN absolute + COMMAND_ARGV=(), prints `[INFO] MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI: <name> -> <abs>`, else CLI_NOT_FOUND refusal. Empty project real path fails closed.
- No re-apply needed: both later parse_command_into_argv calls (~:594, ~:727) run before the resolver; nothing re-parses after it. gemini->agy compares COMMAND_BIN = "gemini", which is never true for an absolute path, so it is skipped under the marker. Account signin-state and codex/grok checks use COMMAND_BIN. bash 3.2 constructs only.
Scope growth (necessary): scripts/tests/postflight.sh R13c2 P rows launched `--command /bin/true` under the marker; this row refuses that (verified: old harness + new wrapper fails P1 with COMMAND_REFUSED). Now `--command claude` with a `$PR/bin/claude` exit-0 stub ($PR/bin is first on PATH, outside the project). Trimmed harness (prologue + [protected runtime]) on a snapshot: `[protected runtime] ok`, rc=0.
Test fixes: a JS default turned `marker: undefined` into '1' (now null = unset); MOE_NODE_COMMAND is a fixture symlink because the wrapper prepends node's dir to PATH (nvm dir holds a real codex).

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.ps1 is the twin, keeping parity with step 2. It stays UTF-8 with BOM (scripts/CLAUDE.md).

Right after `$resolvedCommand = Resolve-CommandParts ...` (~:795-797), and before any MCP config write or daemon RPC, act only when R13c2's protected flag is set:
1. Gate. Accept only when `$Command` is exactly one of claude, codex, gemini, grok (-ceq, case-sensitive) and `$CommandArgs` is empty. Otherwise:
   - write the R1 line through [Console]::Error.WriteLine, byte-identical to sh, with the same sanitizing (control chars replaced, then truncated to 200);
   - exit 1, the way R13c2's gate exits (the supervisor at the top re-exits with 1).
2. Resolve.
   - Split $env:PATH on [IO.Path]::PathSeparator.
   - Skip empty entries and entries that are not fully qualified: a drive root with a separator, UNC, or a leading '/' on non-Windows pwsh.
   - Skip entries inside the project: compare [IO.Path]::GetFullPath on both sides with a separator boundary, case-insensitively on Windows.
   - For the first entry holding `<name>` with a PATHEXT extension (Windows) or the bare name (elsewhere) as a leaf file, set `$Command` to that absolute path and print the INFO line. Otherwise print the CLI_NOT_FOUND line and exit 1.
   - Do NOT use Get-Command: it consults aliases, functions and the module path.
3. Every later use of the CLI reads `$Command`, so they all get the absolute path. `$cmdBase` detection still works through GetFileNameWithoutExtension. A later gemini->agy style substitution under the flag goes through the same resolver, or is skipped.

Error handling:
- GetFullPath or Test-Path exceptions on a malformed PATH entry are caught, and that entry is skipped;
- a refusal writes one line and exits 1 before any write or RPC;
- nothing runs without the flag.

Without the flag, behavior is unchanged. Run `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`. If it pins wrapper strings, add the four new message codes the way it pins R13c2's codes.
implementationPlan.note:
moe-agent.ps1, marker-only (the bytes are in checkpoint 29de0da4, recovered from the prior session's rescue ref; this session reviewed and tested them):
- Gate: Stop-MoeProtectedAgent plus the allowlist check sit right after $script:MoeRuntimeProtected is set. That is ahead of R13c2's path gate, the exit handler and every MCP config write or RPC, which is EARLIER than the plan's 'after Resolve-CommandParts' (~:981): the MCP config and RPCs run before that point, and the sh gate makes the same early choice. -ceq claude|codex|gemini|grok (-cnotin) and an empty -CommandArgs are required. Otherwise the shown value is (Command + CommandArgs) joined with ' ', \p{Cc} -> '?', cut to 200, and [Console]::Error.WriteLine then exit 1. The line is byte-identical to sh.
- Resolve-MoeProtectedCli: a manual scan of $env:PATH split on PathSeparator, quotes trimmed. Windows keeps only drive-rooted or UNC entries; non-Windows keeps only a leading '/'. Get-MoeRealPath follows symlinks and junctions (GetFullPath keeps them). An entry equal to the project's real path, or under it with a separator boundary, is skipped (OrdinalIgnoreCase on Windows). Windows tries .ps1 and then PATHEXT, PowerShell's own order. A malformed entry is caught and skipped. If the project's real path can't be read, the scan stops and NOT_FOUND fails closed.
- A protected $Command is never re-split by Resolve-CommandParts. gemini->agy compares $Command -eq 'gemini', which is never true for an absolute path, so it is skipped. The account signin-state probe passes the extensionless trusted path, so the helper resolves PATHEXT only in that dir.
- postflight.ps1: R13c2's P rows now use -Command claude, with a claude.cmd stub on a prepended $prBin. This scope growth is needed because the gate refuses the old $trueCmd.
- Test harness fix: assertResolved no longer requires code !== 1 on Windows, because taskkill /F leaves exit 1.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of `git diff 03355c25 -- scripts/`: +338/-4 (net 334). No real findings, so nothing changed in this step.

- Exec under the marker:
  - sh: every exec site after the resolver uses "$COMMAND_BIN", which is absolute. That covers the account signin-state (~:7646), the codex argv probe and --version, codex exec/TUI, gemini, grok and the 4 claude sites. agent_git_exec only `exec "$@"`.
  - sh: `$COMMAND` is never used after the resolver. Both parse_command_into_argv re-parses (:594 and :727) are top-level and run before it. parse_command_first_token runs in a $( ) subshell. gemini->agy compares COMMAND_BIN = "gemini", which is never true for an absolute path.
  - ps1: `& $Command` (Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand) and the Get-Command checks on the absolute path. `-eq "gemini"` is skipped. The account probe gets the extensionless trusted path.
- Symlinked PATH dirs:
  - sh: `pwd -P` plus an ancestor walk with `-ef` against the project's `pwd -P` compares inodes. T3's link and '..' rows are covered.
  - ps1: Get-MoeRealPath follows junctions and symlinks per component. T3 passes with a junction on PS 5.1 and pwsh 7.
- Message: only the bounded, sanitized command (or the fixed CLI name) is shown; no env or path values leak. bash 3.2-safe constructs.
- Legacy: every new branch is behind RUNTIME_PROTECTED=1 / $script:MoeRuntimeProtected (exact '1'). The rest of the diff is inert function definitions and a `$null` init; L1 (unset and '01') is green on bash, PS 5.1 and pwsh 7.
- Parity: the same refusedLine/notFoundLine/infoLine strings are asserted for both engines. parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 pass.
- set -e: `|| continue`, `&& continue 2` and the if-wrapped tests are all errexit-safe. Refusals exit at top level (not in a subshell) and clear WORKER_ID, so the EXIT trap deregisters nothing.
- An empty or unreadable project real path fails closed (NOT_FOUND) in both wrappers. A malformed ps1 PATH entry is caught and skipped.

Theoretical ceilings, all host-controlled (PATH and trusted dirs are not repo content):
- (a) a Windows 8.3 short-name spelling of the project in PATH (ponytail comment in ps1);
- (b) a file-level symlink inside a trusted dir pointing into the project;
- (c) on non-Windows pwsh a non-executable leaf can be picked, and its exec then fails closed.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Resolve once, right after the command is parsed, and replace COMMAND_BIN/$Command with the trusted absolute path (chosen). Every later execution site uses the variable, so one swap covers all of them.
- Filtering PATH for the whole wrapper process: rejected. It could change how node, python or git are looked up, which is outside this row's concern.
- `command -v` or Get-Command for the lookup: rejected. The hash table, aliases, functions and modules could answer instead of the filesystem.
- Adding an IDE-supplied trusted token: rejected, because the allowlist plus trusted resolution is enough and simpler.

completionSummary:
With MOE_RUNTIME_PROTECTED exactly '1', moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 run only claude, codex, gemini or grok, by bare name, resolved from an absolute PATH entry outside the project. Without the marker nothing changes.

Messages. Each refusal is one stderr line, byte-identical in both wrappers, followed by exit 1:
- `[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMAND_REFUSED: '<cmd>' is not one of claude, codex, gemini, grok; the protected runtime runs only these agent CLIs by name. Refusing to start.` The value has control chars replaced by '?' and is cut to 200 chars.
- `[ERROR] MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI_NOT_FOUND: <name> was not found on an absolute PATH entry outside the project; refusing to start.`
- On success: `[INFO] MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_CLI: <name> -> <abs>`.

Placement and lookup:
- The allowlist gate runs before CLI detection (sh) or right after the marker is read (ps1), ahead of any MCP config write or RPC.
- The lookup is a manual PATH scan, never command -v or Get-Command. It skips empty, '.', relative and in-project entries: sh compares `pwd -P` with an ancestor `-ef` walk, ps1 follows junctions and symlinks.
- Every later exec, the account signin probe included, uses the absolute path. gemini->agy never fires under the marker.
- R13c2's P rows in postflight.{sh,ps1} now launch a `claude` stub from a trusted bin dir. This scope growth is needed because the gate refuses the old /bin/true.
